_note: The twelve cities, as a first collection rather than a fixed list.
Every other list on this site is derived — the destinations grid, the map,
the footer are all len() of something on disk. This one is curated, and says
so: it is an editor's twelve, not the twelve largest or the twelve anything.
`country` has to be a published slug in tourism/countries/, because the card
links there and a card that links nowhere is not a destination. Luanda is the
one city on the brief that is missing here for exactly that reason: Angola is
not in the atlas, so adding Luanda means adding Angola first — a dataset and a
map outline, not a line in this file.
`photo` is null until there is a real photograph of that city in the repo. It
is never filled with a generated image: these are named, real places, and a
picture of a city that does not exist is a lie about somewhere you can buy a
ticket to. A card with no photograph gets a typographic plate instead, which
is a deliberate treatment rather than a gap, and drops the picture in the

cities.name: Cape Town
cities.say: The only city on earth with a national park through the middle of it. The mountain is inside the municipal boundary, there is an ocean on either side, and the winelands start forty minutes from the centre.
cities.alt: The V&A Waterfront in Cape Town at midday, yachts and quaysides in the foreground and Table Mountain and Devil's Peak rising directly behind the city centre

cities.name: Marrakech
cities.say: Eleven centuries inside one set of walls. Jemaa el-Fna empties and refills twice a day — orange carts and storytellers in the afternoon, a hundred food stalls after dark, and the Atlas on the skyline behind it.
cities.alt: Jemaa el-Fna square in Marrakech at dusk, crowds moving between rows of covered food stalls, the pink walls of the medina and a minaret behind, with the sky going orange

cities.name: Lagos
cities.say: The loudest cultural output on the continent, and most of it made in the last twenty years: Afrobeats, Nollywood, a gallery and fashion scene exporting worldwide, across a city of twenty million on a lagoon.
cities.alt: The Lagos Marina waterfront seen from above, the lagoon on the left and the towers and traffic of Lagos Island running along the shoreline

cities.name: Nairobi
cities.say: The only capital with a national park on its boundary — lion and rhino within sight of the towers — and the tech corridor that got the country called Silicon Savannah.
cities.alt: Central Nairobi from the air on a clear day, towers and older colonial-era rooftops in the foreground and the city spreading to the horizon under cumulus cloud

cities.name: Accra
cities.say: Where a great deal of contemporary African design and music is actually being made, on an Atlantic coast with the forts of the slave trade a couple of hours west of it.

cities.name: Addis Ababa
cities.say: Two and a half thousand metres up, in the one African country never colonised — which is why the national museum, the cuisine and the calendar are all their own.
cities.alt: Bole Road in Addis Ababa at dusk, glass towers and lit shopfronts along a wide avenue with evening traffic and people crossing

cities.name: Kigali
cities.say: Built across a set of ridges and quiet in a way no city this size has any right to be. The coffee is grown within sight of it and the memorial is not optional.

cities.name: Dakar
cities.say: The westernmost city on the continent, and the one that exported mbalax and a contemporary art biennale. Gorée is twenty minutes offshore.

cities.name: Abidjan
cities.say: Built around a lagoon and out of it — the economic engine of francophone West Africa, with the architecture, the food and the nights that come with that.
cities.alt: The Boulevard Valery Giscard d'Estaing interchange in Abidjan from the air, traffic looping through a raised roundabout with the Plateau towers and the Ebrie lagoon behind it

cities.name: Maputo
cities.say: Acacia avenues, Portuguese modernism and an Indian Ocean seafood culture, on a bay at the southern end of two thousand kilometres of coast.

cities.name: Douala
cities.say: The Wouri estuary, the port that most of central Africa's freight goes through, makossa, and the city half this site's enquiries are answered from.

_routes_note: Three journeys, drawn as paths across the map rather than listed as itineraries.
A waypoint is a real place with real coordinates; it does not need a card in the
collection to be somewhere the road goes through. Kampala, Windhoek and Victoria
Falls are waypoints, not cities in the twelve.

routes.name: The Gulf of Guinea
routes.line: Lagos to Abidjan, along the coast the whole way

routes.name: Across the Rift
routes.line: Nairobi to Kigali, over the escarpment and around the lake

routes.name: Cape to Zambezi
routes.line: Cape Town to the falls, most of it gravel
